sentences.text: Scutarx was a medium-sized, heavily armored reptile belonging to the herbivorous clade Aetosauria, distinguished from other members by a large, triangular boss on the dorsal surface of its osteoderms.

Unlike other aetosaurs, the frontal bone of Scutarx lacks a distinct, elevated midline ridge, while a distinctive triangular protuberance on the posteromedial corner of the osteoderms helps identify the species Scutarx deltatylus. The triangular protuberance on cervical osteoderms is shaped like a right triangle, unlike the equilateral triangles found in the trunk series.

Scutarx deltatylus lacks the "tongue-and-groove" lateral articular surfaces common in other aetosaurs, though the scalloping of the anterior bar on its osteoderms remains a shared characteristic found in all aetosaurs.
Scutarx measured between one and three meters in length and served as one of the earliest large herbivorous archosaurs of the Late Triassic.

A mid-trunk vertebra of Scutarx has a centrum that is 45.78 mm long and 41.81 mm tall, with the neural spine measuring 32.3 mm long, which is shorter than the centrum height. The prezygapophyses of Scutarx vertebrae are inclined at approximately 45 degrees from the horizontal.

The genus Scutarx was described by William G. Parker in 2016, with fossils found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona and the Cooper Canyon Formation of Texas. Four partial skeletons of Scutarx, including the carapace and girdles, were collected between 2002 and 2009.

In posterior trunk vertebrae, the centra of Scutarx are taller than they are long. Scutarx possesses a robust sacral rib that extends laterally to touch the ilium, and the anterior and mid-trunk ribs are double-headed. The pubis of Scutarx deltatylus uniquely features two large pubic foremen, a trait found in only one other aetosaur.

Scutarx is classified within the family Stagonolepididae and the clade Aetosauriformes, belonging to the parent group Desmatosuchinae. Phylogenetic analysis identifies Scutarx as the sister taxon to Adamanasuchus and Calyptosuchus within the clade Desmatosuchinae.
The type species of the genus Scutarx is Scutarx deltatylus.
Scutarx lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
